: NSAIDs Role in AKI\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-Adverse renal effects from the NSAIDS are caused by two distinct pathologies .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1).AKI from NSAIDS is due to reduced renal plasma flow caused by decrease in prostaglandins,which regulates the vasodilation at the glomerular level.NSAIDS disrupt the compensatory vasodilation at glomerular level.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2).AKI is acute interstitial nephritis,which is characterized by the presence of inflammatory cell infiltrates in interstitium of kidney .Acute interstitial nephritis caused by immunological reaction after NSAID exposure of about a week.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2).
